title: Touch hit area & token contrast sweep: Safari/Firefox mobile gesture regressions
creator: Sofia Rivera
description: Scope: run an exhaustive QA sweep focused on touch hit areas (buttons, compact controls, table row actions), token-driven contrast regressions, and gesture edge cases in Safari iOS and Firefox Mobile. Goal is to identify regressions introduced by recent token compression and compact mode changes, classify them, and deliver prioritized fixes and design deltas for engineering. This ticket bundles discovery, reproducible steps, design fixes, and handoff artifacts for small-to-medium fixes (estimated 5 points). Exclusions: deep layout engine fixes that require engine-level work; those will be logged as dependencies.
acceptance_criteria: Catalog of unique cross-browser/mobile issues with repro steps and severity
Design deltas (Figma frames + token overrides) for each P0/P1 cosmetic issue
QA verification checklist and automated visual regression targets added to the UI-kit snapshot suite
PRs opened for each fix with design review comments addressed
Handoff notes for ENG tickets that are out of scope (layout engine/renderer-level)
steps_to_reproduce: Open app shell in Safari on iOS 16/17 using responsive viewport 375x812; enable compact density in settings
Navigate to Dashboard -> Reports table; attempt to select row action menu via touch when table is vertically scrolled
Observe hit area mismatch between visual token and effective touch region (touch misses on fast swipes)
Repeat in Firefox Android and compare: note differences in momentum scrolling and sticky header overlap on table actions
Run the same flows with reduced token spacing (--compact-token-scale) to see when buttons overlap or collapse into icon-only states
Use VoiceOver/TalkBack to validate accessibility focus ring and contrast thresholds for token-driven color changes
recent_comments: 2026-03-03 - Sofia Rivera: Initial exploration found 6 distinct issues across buttons/tables/charts; most reproducible in Safari iOS when compact tokens are active.

2026-03-05 - Aisha Patel: Narrowed down two root causes: (1) token margin collapse when density < 0.75, (2) z-index/touch-surface clipping for sticky table headers. Drafted quick-fix spec for token margins.
2026-03-07 - Markus Chen (ENG): Proposed engineering mitigation: add an explicit hit-surface layer for compact buttons and adjust pointer-events handling. Will prototype as small patch, ETA 48 hours.
2026-03-11 - Sofia Rivera: Pushed Figma deltas for button hit-surface and updated token scale recommendations. Uploaded accessibility contrast report. Requesting design review from Lila.
2026-03-13 - Lila Moreno (Design Lead): Reviewed and approved deltas for buttons and table row actions. Flagged chart tooltip overlap as a separate low-priority task.
2026-03-14 - Aisha Patel: Opened PR #5423 with hit-surface layer changes and unit snapshots. QA in progress; Firefox-specific tweak pending. Linking PR in artifacts.
notes: Trade-off: we prefer a lightweight hit-surface overlay to avoid changing global token APIs—this minimizes churn for downstream teams but adds a minor DOM element per compact control.
Decision: implement hit-surface only for compact density and when accessible-touch targets fall below 44px; document token min-values in spec.
Follow-up: ENG to evaluate cost of adding touch-surface for virtualized tables with 1000+ rows; if expensive, fallback is to increase compact token min-height for table rows only.
QA checklist: include iOS Safari (13/14/16/17), Firefox Android latest, Chrome Android latest, plus low-end Android device (2GB RAM) smoke test.
